title: Nutrition and Stress
subtitle: Stress eating, cortisol, appetite, and practical dietary strategies
evidence_strength: Moderate evidence supports the hormonal and behavioral links between stress and nutrition, with emerging clinical trials investigating dietary interventions for stress-related eating. Multiple observational studies confirm associations among cortisol, appetite changes, and metabolic outcomes, though interindividual variability exists. Nutritional guidance is underpinned by robust general dietary principles adapted to stress contexts. More high-quality randomized trials are needed to clarify specific food effects on stress hormones and long-term outcomes.
review_status: AI draft - scientific, clinical, and editorial review required
